chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Mu'addib narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Qutayba ibn Sa'id, from 'Amr ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Muslim. He said:

He said: I went out with al-Hasan al-Basri and Anas ibn Malik until we came to the door of Umm Salama (may Allah be pleased with her). Anas sat at the door, and I entered with al-Hasan al-Basri. I heard al-Hasan saying: Peace be upon you, O mother, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. She said to him: And upon you be peace. Who are you, my son?

He said: I am al-Hasan al-Basri. She said: What have you come for, O Hasan? He said to her: I have come so that you may narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).

So Umm Salama said: By Allah, I will surely narrate to you a hadith that my ears heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) — and if I did not, then may they become deaf; and my eyes saw it — and if they did not, then may they become blind; and my heart preserved it — and if it did not, then may Allah seal it; and may my tongue be muted if I did not hear the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say to Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him): O Ali! There is no servant who meets Allah on the Day he meets Him while denying your wilaya, except that he meets Allah as a worshipper of idols or graven images.

He (Abu Muslim) said: So I heard al-Hasan al-Basri saying: Allah is the Greatest! I bear witness that Ali is my master and the master of the believers. When he (al-Hasan) left, Anas ibn Malik said to him: Why do I see you reciting the takbir? He said: I asked our mother Umm Salama to narrate to me a hadith that she had heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) regarding Ali (peace be upon him).

So she said to me such-and-such. So I said: Allah is the Greatest! I bear witness that Ali is my master and the master of every believer. He (Abu Muslim) said: So at that, I heard Anas ibn Malik saying: I bear witness upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that he said this statement three or four times.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Takbir — Allah is the Greatest; exclamation of awe and affirmation
key_terms.جَاحِد: One who denies/rejects despite knowing the truth; stronger than mere ignorance
key_terms.صَنَم: Idol — a carved or sculpted image worshipped besides God
key_terms.وَثَن: Graven image/idol — any object of idolatrous worship
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilaya — divinely appointed guardianship and authority; here referring specifically to the wilaya of Imam Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Umm Salama narrate about the wilaya of Imam Ali according to Al-Amali of al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates how al-Hasan al-Basri visited Umm Salama (RA), wife of the Prophet, seeking a hadith about Imam Ali (AS). Umm Salama solemnly swore — invoking her ears, eyes, heart, and tongue as witnesses — that she heard the Prophet say: anyone who meets God denying the wilaya (guardianship/authority) of Ali will meet God as an idol-worshipper. The hadith was corroborated by Anas ibn Malik who testified that the Prophet made this declaration three or four times, highlighting the central Shia doctrine of the wilaya of Imam Ali.
